# The board

> Every request to the editor and every task on SHarness, numbered, with its owner and its status; one file per row.

*Source: <https://sharness.ai/admin/board/index.html> · generated by tools/gen_admin.py from content/admin/, so the page and this file cannot drift. Every page on this site has a .md twin.*

---

Every piece of work on SHarness as one row, numbered so it can be referred to from any page, commit or conversation, and never renumbered. **R** is a request: it needs the editor (a decision, a key, a setting) and says what it blocks. **T** is a task: work a member has or anyone can pick up. One file per row under `content/admin/board/`; the [Sherpa](../members/sherpa/index.md) keeps the rows honest and scopes them into releases, the [conductor](../members/conductor/index.md) builds this page from them, and anyone opens a row by adding a file ([how](../guidance/index.md)). 11 request(s) wait on the editor and 22 task(s) are open, as of 26 Oct 2026.

| T21 | **Two releases pushed seconds apart leave dev stuck: the cancelled run never tags, and the next one is refused.** Seen on 26 October 2026 at 01:32 UTC. dev@'s v0.5.33 was pushed at 01:31:56 while v0.5.32's run was deploying; website@'s v0.5.34 followed at 01:32:08. The workflow's `concurrency: pages` group keeps one run in progress and **one** pending, so GitHub cancelled the pending v0.5.33 run when v0.5.34's queued (`cancel-in-progress: false` protects only the running one). v0.5.33 was never tagged, and v0.5.34's `tag-release` job refused itself: "latest tag is v0.5.32, expected v0.5.33, got v0.5.34". Every later release would have been refused the same way, since `tools/ship.py` bumps from the newest of the tag and dev's `version.txt`. Unstuck by hand at 01:40: website@ re-ran v0.5.33's run (tagged and deployed), then v0.5.34's (tagged, live at 01:44). Nothing was lost; the live site served v0.5.32 for twelve minutes. **A second way in, 26 October 2026, 01:43 to 02:00 UTC** (cli@'s c2850bc): a release whose tip was a merge commit, not the `site v0.5.39:` commit (a release-row conflict resolved by hand instead of with `tools/ship.py`). `tag-release` looks for the newest commit whose subject starts `site v<version>:`, found v0.5.38's, and refused; v0.5.40 and v0.5.41 were refused in turn. cli@ pushed a commit CI could tag as v0.5.39, then v0.5.40's and v0.5.41's runs were re-run in order; v0.5.41 was live by 02:05. The proposed fix below covers this case too. The fix is in `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`, so it goes to security@ for review and needs the editor's go before it lands. Proposed: the `tag-release` job tags every `site vX.Y.Z:` release commit in the pushed range that has no tag yet, oldest first, before the patch check, so a cancelled run's release is tagged by the next run; the check stays strict for the newest. Until then: a release whose run is refused this way is unstuck by re-running the cancelled run, then the refused one, in that order. **26 Oct 2026, later:** R23 (decided by the editor) replaces the check this row proposed to loosen: CI assigns the number from the tags inside the release job and tags its own commit, so a dropped queued run and a merge-commit tip can no longer leave a release untagged; the release job is in `deploy-pages.yml` for website@ to own and security@ to review. (opened 2026-10-26) | website | open |
| T23 | **sharness-ai decide, the decision engine: a command, a policy, a directory and an intent in; allow, deny or ask out.** From [the decision at the door](../../design/decision/index.md) §4 and §7, at the editor's direction of 26 Oct 2026. The engine maps a shell command to the rows of the policy the process runs under and answers allow (every row held), deny (a row refused, a behaviour row broken, or a command it cannot read: unknown is no) or ask (a row the policy cannot hold), with a one-line summary in UX-059's shape (reads, writes, network, reversible) and, for ask, a question in the person's words with three choices (once, add the row, refuse). Deterministic: the same command under the same policy gets the same answer. Intent is carried into the question and never changes the verdict. The verdict carries the harness's PreToolUse hook form, so it can sit behind a hook today (a Setting) and inside sharness.bash later (a Boundary). A 99-line prototype with twelve sample commands is on the CLI repository's branch pbp/decide-prototype under experiments/decide/, to take or replace; every verdict needs a test. Pairs with T22 (the level-3 form, so that "ask" for a host becomes a row the policy can hold). (opened 2026-10-26) | cli | open |
| T24 | **sharness-ai rehearse: the command run first in a twin of the workspace, no network, traced; the verdict from the facts.** From [the decision at the door](../../design/decision/index.md) §10 and §11, at the editor's direction of 26 Oct 2026 ("simulate the installation, almost like a sandbox"). A copy of the workspace as the twin (`sharness.fs.disk.twin` in its cheapest form; copy-on-write later), a rehearsal policy derived from the real one (the twin the only writable place, `network: "none"`), `sharness-ai run` with `strace -f`, and a report of what the command tried: writes inside, writes refused outside, connects refused, deletes, processes. Verdict: a refused write outside is deny; a network attempt, a delete or a timeout is ask, with the facts in the question; otherwise allow; refused reads reported, never judged. The sketch is `experiments/decide/rehearse.py` on the CLI branch pbp/decide-prototype (82 lines; known gap: child execve lines split by strace are missed, so programs run are undercounted). Pairs with T23 (the parse) and gives `decide` its second source of truth. (opened 2026-10-26) | cli | open |
| T25 | **Review of MVP 1 and MVP 2 (CLI dev at cf2ea3d): four bugs in the door kit and sharness.fs, one wording fix in contain.** website@sharness reviewed the CLI's `dev` at cf2ea3d on 26 Oct 2026, at the editor's request: 3392842 (MVP 1, the levels), 5421d4e (MVP 2, the first door) and the commits after them, including cli@'s own review 1. The 209 tests pass (Python 3.13, this session). Each finding below was reproduced against a running door or the module, not only read; the scripts are small and can become tests. security@ is asked to look at 1 and 2 first. 1. **The secret scan is quadratic** (`sharness_ai/door/Rows.py`, the vault-key shape `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}:…`). On a body that is one long run of letters, digits, `_` or `-` the regex retries the greedy run from every start position: 16 KB took 0.33 s, 32 KB 1.25 s, 64 KB 5.2 s (measured 26 Oct 2026); 1 MB would be about 20 minutes and `max_bytes` allows 64 MiB. Any caller with the `app` certificate can hold a door thread and a core; an honest large write of hex or base64url times out at the client (10 s) while the door still writes it. Fix: `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_-])` before the run, which starts a match only where a run starts: 1 MB in 17 ms, and keys are still found. The site's own gate had the same pattern (`tools/validate.js`, `tools/ship.py`) and carries the fix from the release that opened this row. 2. **One idle TCP connection freezes the door** (`sharness_ai/door/Door.py`, `serve()`). The listening socket is wrapped with `server_side=True`, so the TLS handshake happens inside `accept()` on the single serving thread, before `Handler.timeout` applies. A local process with no certificate that connects and sends nothing stops every other caller until it hangs up: reproduced, a `GET /v0/hello` from a valid `app` timed out after 10 s while one bare socket was open, and answered 200 once it closed. Fix: wrap each accepted socket with `do_handshake_on_connect=False` and do the handshake in the request's thread under the 30 s timeout (override `get_request`/`finish_request`). 3. **`refuse_secrets` is bypassed by splitting a secret across appends** (`Rows.verdict` sees only the new body; `FS.handle` append). `POST …/notes.txt/append` with `-----BEGIN PRIVATE ` then `KEY-----` both return 201 and the file holds the header. Fix: on append, scan the last few hundred bytes of the existing file together with the new bytes (the longest shape bounds the window). 4. **Concurrent writes to one path all fail** (`sharness_ai/fs/disk/Disk.py`, `write`). The temporary name is `.sharness-fs-<pid>-<name>.tmp`, the same for every thread of the threaded server; the second writer's `O_EXCL` fails and its cleanup unlinks the first writer's temporary file, whose rename then fails: 8 of 8 concurrent writers failed (`FileExistsError`, `FileNotFoundError`). Fix: a random suffix (`secrets.token_hex(8)`) and unlink only the name this call created. A long file name also overflows 255 bytes once the prefix is added. 5. **A binary file does not read back** (`FS.handle`, read): the content is decoded as UTF-8 with replacement characters, so bytes above 0x7f are lost while `size` reports the true length. Fix: `content_b64` when the bytes are not UTF-8. 6. **Wording on `contain` and `explain`** (`sharness_ai/cli/CLI__Level.py`, `_report_lines`): "held: N rows by the kernel: files, ports, caps; nothing else is reachable" is printed directly above "not held: github.com: held as port 443; the host name is not held", so the screen says nothing else is reachable while every host on 443 is, and UDP and Unix sockets are listed as not covered on the next line. Suggested: "held: N rows by the kernel: files, ports, caps" and, when there are unheld rows, nothing more. Smaller: `L3.site` drops a path silently (`github.com/x` is accepted as `github.com`) though its error text says "no path". Checked and sound: the edge matrix (a valid `net` certificate is refused on `fs`), the `openat` walk with `O_NOFOLLOW`, keys born 0600 and the CA key destroyed in a `finally`, `contain` running the child with `--expect-hash` on the chain's level-2 hash and removing its temporary policy after the fork returns, `Verdict.clean` on every echoed string. Published on [sharness.fs §5](../../components/fs/index.md#5-known-issues-as-of-28-oct-2026); the page moves each row to fixed when its fix lands on `dev`. **Re-test, 28 Oct 2026 (website@, CLI `dev` at 8210807, run from the installed wheel and the source tree).** Fixed in 4a0bdd3, each reproduction re-run: items 1 (linear scan), 2 (the handshake no longer freezes the door), 4 (16 concurrent writers all got 201). Still reproduce: item 3 (a secret split across two appends is stored; the door's `REALITY.md` now lists it as not covered), item 5 (binary read-back: 256 bytes written, 512 returned) and item 6 (`contain` still prints "nothing else is reachable" above the unheld host line; `L3.site('github.com/x')` still returns `github.com`). New on `dev` since: the network door and `sharness-ai shell` (63360be); its refusals were checked and held (an unlisted host refused by the door, a bypass and a raw connect refused by the kernel). The allowlist matcher held against 23 tricky host names (suffix tricks, userinfo, IP literals in decimal and hex, unicode, NUL, `%00`). One cosmetic note: inside the shell `sh` prints `cannot create /dev/null: Permission denied` because the shell's policy has no write right on `/dev/null`. (opened 2026-10-26) | cli | open |

The first step is a level-3 form: `sites: [github.com, api.anthropic.com]` compiled deterministically into the ports the kernel holds today (443, and the gap, hostnames, named as unheld until `net` exists), with the hash of the level-3 document carried beside the hash of its expansion. Follows T14 (the row shape). **Done, 26 Oct 2026 (cli):** the level-3 form (`network.sites`, host names compiled to the ports the kernel holds, the names reported as unheld; a `connect_tcp_ports` row beside them passed through and marked), levels 4 and 5 as compilers (`profile`, `contain`), `explain` down the chain with one hash per level, and the report in the person's nouns (held, not held, passed through, not covered) on `contain` and `explain`. On the CLI's `dev` as 3392842. Not done: the grant-minus-mandate count ("N things you did not ask for"), which needs the grant measured against the mandate; `hello` itself still reports its six probes as before.
